brief: The canvas presents a colossal, three-dimensional cross-section into the mineralized skeleton of a leviathan. Massive, curving ribs and vertebrae emerge from the deep, perpetually dissolving into fine particulate matter. Deep turquoise and sepia tones dominate, highlighted by the oxidizing reds and ochres of calcium carbonate erosion. The structure appears to be caught in an eternal, slow collapse, where grand, monumental curves slowly flake away and sift into the abyssal sediment. The viewer witnesses the slow, geological passage of time as perfect geometry yields to crystalline decay.

statement: This sketch presents a geological visualization of a submerged leviathan's mineralized skeleton undergoing slow decay. Through the use of 3D geometry and dynamic lighting, it depicts the gradual collapse of massive ribcage structures into fine particulate matter. The interplay of deep turquoise and sepia tones, punctuated by oxidizing reds and ochres, captures the essence of calcium carbonate erosion over geological time. The viewer witnesses the slow dissolution of these monumental forms, where grand curves slowly flake away into sediment, creating an atmosphere of eternal transformation. The simulation uses a particle-based system to model structural breakdown, with fragments splitting and drifting according to physics-based motion, embodying both the monumentality and fragility of ancient mineralized remains.
